condition: Status List Token in JWT; exp and ttl are RECOMMENDED only
quote: typ: REQUIRED. The JWT type MUST be statuslist+jwt ... exp: RECOMMENDED ... ttl: RECOMMENDED
correction: Notes require "exp and ttl"; draft-21 makes both RECOMMENDED, not required.

condition: Only when the status_list mechanism is used
quote: status_list: REQUIRED when the status mechanism defined in this specification is used.

condition: Status Provider responses
quote: In the successful response, the Status Provider MUST use the following content-type: * "application/statuslist+jwt" for Status List Token in JWT format * "application/statuslist+cwt" for Status List Token in CWT format ...

condition: Only re-issued or batch-issued Referenced Tokens
quote: every Referenced Token MUST have a dedicated Status List entry and MAY be spread across multiple Status List Tokens.

condition: Preventing all double allocation is RECOMMENDED; unintended double allocation MUST be prevented
quote: The Status Issuer MUST prevent any unintended double allocation.
The Issuer MUST include the typ header parameter in the SD-JWT. The typ value MUST use dc+sd-jwt

condition: "equal to the configuration" comes from OID4VCI A.3.2
quote: vct: REQUIRED. The type of the Verifiable Digital Credential, e.g., https://credentials.example.com/identity_credential, as defined in Section 2.2.2.1

verified_at: ISO/IEC 18013-5 not accessible (paywalled); OID4VCI A.2.4 checked: https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_0.html (1.0 Final, 16 Sep 2025)
correction: Could not verify against ISO/IEC 18013-5 text; OID4VCI A.2.4 only requires the base64url IssuerSigned structure.

condition: ISO/IEC 18013-5 is paywalled
verified_at: ISO/IEC 18013-5 not accessible (paywalled); OID4VCI A.2.4 checked: https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_0.html (1.0 Final, 16 Sep 2025)
correction: Could not verify against ISO/IEC 18013-5 text.

condition: Unconditional under HAIP §4.1 ("The Authorization Server MUST support metadata according to [RFC8414]")
quote: Authorization servers supporting metadata MUST make a JSON document containing metadata as specified in Section 2 available at a path formed by inserting a well-known URI string into the authorization ...

condition: "never 5xx" is implied by the 400 default
quote: The authorization server responds with an HTTP 400 (Bad Request) status code (unless specified ... error REQUIRED. A single ASCII [USASCII] error code from the following

condition: Bearer-token resources only; 401 for invalid_token is SHOULD; for DPoP-bound tokens RFC 9449 §7.1 says the server "can respond with a challenge"; OID4VCI §8.3.1.1 cites RFC 6750 §3 only "such as"
quote: the resource server MUST include the HTTP "WWW-Authenticate" response header field;
correction: Overstated for HAIP/DPoP issuers: the MUST is the Bearer challenge header; the 401 status is SHOULD, and DPoP challenges are optional.

condition: Only when a 405 is sent (then an Allow header is required)
quote: The origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405 response containing a list of the target resource's currently supported methods.
correction: RFC 9110 does not mandate 405 for wrong methods; "refused without 5xx" is hardening.

condition: Flows that use the authorization endpoint (HAIP §4: PAR where the authorization endpoint is used)
quote: For flows that use the authorization endpoint, authorization servers ... shall reject authorization requests sent without [RFC9126];
correction: RFC 9126 §4 lets an AS require PAR and refuse with invalid_request; §5 defines require_pushed_authorization_requests.

condition: PAR endpoint (FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.2 item 2)
quote: The authorization server MUST process the request as follows: 1. Authenticate the client in the same way as at the token endpoint ... 2. Reject the request if the "request_uri" authorization request parameter is provided.
correction: The 201 answer with request_uri and expires_in is §2.2; the PAR endpoint URL must use https (§2).

condition: PAR endpoint
quote: The "request_uri" value MUST be bound to the client that posted the authorization request.
correction: Single use is a SHOULD in RFC 9126 §4 and §7.3; an expired request_uri MUST be rejected (§4), and FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.2 item 12 requires expires_in under 600 s. cunho makes request_uri single use, as the M3 plan proposes (owner decision 13).

condition: Authorization code flow (PKCE required by FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.2 item 5)
quote: If the values are not equal, an error response indicating "invalid_grant" as described in Section 5.2 of [RFC6749] MUST be returned.
correction: The missing-challenge error (invalid_request) is §4.4.1; the 43-128 unreserved characters are §4.1.

condition: Authorization code flow
quote: shall issue authorization codes with a maximum lifetime of 60 seconds;
correction: Reuse is refused by FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.2 item 9. Revoking what a reused code yielded is a SHOULD in RFC 6749 §4.1.2; cunho does it.

condition: PAR with DPoP (FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 item 12)
quote: If both mechanisms are used at the same time, the authorization server MUST reject the request if the JWK Thumbprint in dpop_jkt does not match the public key in the DPoP header.
correction: The two mechanisms are dpop_jkt in the PAR body and a DPoP proof on the PAR request (§10.1); either binds the code, and the token request must prove the same key (§10).

condition: Authorization code flow
quote: When comparing client redirection URIs against pre-registered URIs, authorization servers MUST utilize exact string matching except for port numbers in localhost redirection URIs of native apps
correction: Wallets are not pre-registered. RFC 9126 §2.4 lets an AS accept redirect URIs from authenticated clients at PAR (MAY); what cunho matches against is owner decision 5, still open. FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.2 item 6 requires redirect_uri in PAR and item 8 forbids http except loopback; RFC 6749 §4.1.3 requires the token request to repeat it identically.

condition: Authorization code flow (FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.2 item 7)
quote: In authorization responses to the client, including error responses, an authorization server supporting this specification MUST indicate its identity by including the iss parameter in the response.
correction: §2.3: an AS that publishes RFC 8414 metadata MUST set authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported to true.

condition: Flows that use the authorization endpoint
quote: For flows that use the authorization endpoint, authorization servers shall require the value of response_type described in [RFC6749] to be code;

condition: Redirects from the authorization endpoint and the login
quote: shall not use the HTTP 307 status code when redirecting a request that contains user credentials to avoid forwarding the credentials to a third party accidentally
correction: Using 303 is a SHOULD (item 11); cunho answers 303.

condition: Credential endpoint (FAPI 2.0 resource server)
quote: Resource servers with the FAPI endpoints ... shall not accept access tokens in the query parameters stated in Section 2.3 of OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Usage [RFC6750];
correction: Verified: the rule is FAPI 2.0 Final §5.3.4 (Requirements for resource servers), second item; the M3 plan had no section number.

condition: Authorization code flow
quote: If the resource owner denies the access request or if the request fails for reasons other than a missing or invalid redirection URI, the authorization server informs the client
correction: The sentence has no keyword; error is REQUIRED, and state is REQUIRED when the request carried one (§4.1.2.1). That a failed login never gives a 500 is cunho's rule (DESIGN.md §3).

condition: PAR and token endpoints
quote: Wallets MUST use, and Issuers MUST require, an OAuth2 Client authentication mechanism at OAuth2 Endpoints that support client authentication (such as the PAR and Token Endpoints).
correction: The issuer side of EIDAS-2979-AnnexIb-TR-WIA-3, which binds the wallet. draft-07 §10.3 adds the refresh token request.

condition: Attestations in the format of OID4VCI Appendix E
quote: if applicable, the client_id value in the PAR request MUST be the string in the sub value in the client attestation JWT.
correction: draft-07 §6.3 (token) and §6.4 (PAR) also require the PoP iss to match; the M3 plan cited §6.2, but in -07 the client_id checks are §6.3, §6.4 and §9 step 13.

condition: Client attestation PoP at PAR and token endpoints
quote: shall only accept its issuer identifier value (as defined in [RFC8414]) as a string in the aud claim received in client authentication assertions;
correction: The iat window (accept up to 10 s ahead, refuse more than 60 s ahead) is FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 item 13. The M3 plan cited draft-07 §6.2 steps 7, 8, 10; in -07 the numbered checks are §9 (step 9 the iat window, step 10 the aud), and §6.2 has three header checks. Replay detection by jti is a SHOULD in draft-07 §12.1; cunho refuses a reused jti, as it does for DPoP.

condition: Client attestation at PAR and token endpoints
quote: Upon receiving a Client Attestation, the receiving server MUST ensure the following conditions and rules: ... The key contained in the cnf claim of the Client Attestation JWT is not a private key.
correction: This is §9 step 6; the M3 plan cited §6.2 step 5. Limiting cnf to the agreed curves is cunho's policy, as §9 step 4 leaves algorithms to local policy.

condition: At issuance; the 24-hour re-check of live PIDs is M4
quote: In addition, the PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL validate that the WIA is not revoked.
correction: The M3 plan gave MUST for PID Providers and MAY for Attestation Providers. ARF 3.0.0 WUA_25 says SHALL for both at issuance, and CIR 2025/1569 REQ-EAASP-4.2.2.3-03 says shall for QEAA and PuB-EAA providers. The MAY in TS3 §2.3.1 is about repeating the check during the PID's life, not about issuance. So this row is MUST for every issuer type.

condition: Only if authorization_details is supported (OID4VCI §5.1.1: MAY)
quote: authorization_details: REQUIRED when the authorization_details parameter, as defined in Section 5.1.1, is used in either the Authorization Request or Token Request.

condition: Scope is MAY in OID4VCI §5.1.2; HAIP §4.1 and §4.3 make it how a Wallet names the Credential Type
quote: Credential Issuers MUST interpret each scope value as a request to access the Credential Endpoint as defined in Section 8 for the issuance of a Credential type identified by that scope value.
correction: OID4VCI §5.1.2 also says Credential Issuers MUST ignore unknown scope values, and that authorization_details wins when both request the same Credential type. HAIP §4.3 binds the Wallet (the scope value MUST map to a specific Credential Type); a unique scope per configuration, checked at startup, is how cunho makes that hold.

condition: Only offers that carry issuer_state (OPTIONAL, OID4VCI §4.1.1)
quote: When processing the Authorization Request, the Credential Issuer MUST take into account that the issuer_state is not guaranteed to originate from this Credential Issuer in all circumstances.
correction: Single use and binding to the offer are cunho's way of taking it into account.

condition: Issuer-initiated flows (HAIP §4)
quote: The Grant Type authorization_code MUST be supported as defined in Section 4.1.1 in [OIDF.OID4VCI]
correction: Verified the HAIP §4.2 wording on scope: For Grant Type authorization_code, the Issuer MUST include a scope value in order to allow the Wallet to identify the desired Credential Type. OID4VCI §4.1.1 defines no scope member for this grant (only issuer_state and authorization_server); the Wallet takes the scope from the metadata entry of each credential_configuration_ids value (§4.1.1, §5.1.2), and VCI.META.SCOPE_PER_CONFIG already gives every configuration one. So the offer carries no scope.

condition: When refresh tokens are issued (HAIP §4.4: RECOMMENDED; ARF ISSU_63 asks for re-issuance)
quote: Authorization servers issuing a refresh token ... MUST bind the refresh token to the Client Instance and its associated public key, and NOT just the client
correction: RFC 9449 §5 does not bind the refresh token of an authenticated client to the DPoP key, since client authentication already constrains it; binding it to the DPoP key as well is cunho's choice, as the M3 plan and the ARF ISSU_65 note propose. No rotation: FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 item 9.

condition: Authorization code flow offered
quote: authorization_endpoint URL of the authorization server's authorization endpoint [RFC6749]. This is REQUIRED unless no grant types are supported that use the authorization endpoint.
correction: draft-07 §10.1: the two client attestation alg lists MUST be published when token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported includes attest_jwt_client_auth, which itself is a SHOULD. RFC 9207 §2.3 and RFC 9126 §5 add authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported and the PAR fields.

condition: Signed metadata is MAY in OID4VCI; HAIP §4.1 requires it where ecosystem policy needs issuer authentication beyond TLS (ARF ISSU_22, ISSU_32)
quote: The Credential Issuer MUST support returning metadata in an unsigned form 'application/json' and MAY support returning it in a signed form 'application/jwt'.
correction: HAIP 1.0 §4.1 points to Section 11.2.3 in OID4VCI for signed metadata. In OID4VCI 1.0 Final signed metadata is §12.2.3, and §11.2 is the Successful Notification Response, so HAIP's reference is to an earlier draft's numbering.

condition: Only a provider that has a minimum remaining revocation maintenance period for WIAs
quote: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider having minimum requirements regarding the remaining revocation maintenance period for Wallet Instances (in WIAs) ... SHALL communicate these requirements to the Wallet Unit
correction: TS3 v1.5.2 §2.4 names the field preferred_client_status_period, at the top level of the Credential Issuer metadata, and §2.4.2 puts the duty to honour it on the Wallet Unit. Refusing a WIA with a shorter remaining period is cunho's check, so the stated preference holds.

condition: Reading a LoTE (TRUST.LOTE_PARSER_119602)
quote: LoTE with a Next update occurring in the past shall be discarded as expired as a measure to reduce the risk of a substitution by an attacker with an old LoTE.
correction: The other checks: the signer's Country code and Organization match Scheme Territory and a Scheme operator name (§6.8.0); the sequence number is never recycled to a lower value (§6.3.2); the wallet providers list is a compact JAdES Baseline B signature (Annex E.4, ETSI TS 119 182-1) with LoTEType EUWalletProvidersList (Table E.1). The signer's certificate comes from the OJEU, which the Commission publishes (ARF TLPub_06, TLPub_07).

condition: Certificates on a WIA or KA path whose status comes from a CRL distribution point or OCSP
quote: OCSP clients SHALL confirm that: 1. The certificate identified in a received response corresponds to the certificate that was identified in the corresponding request; 2. The signature on the response is valid;
correction: RFC 5280 §6.1.3(a)(3) lets the status come from a CRL, other status information or out-of-band means; fetching from distribution points (§4.2.1.13) is how cunho obtains it for chains from the LoTE. Authorised responders: RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2. Treating an UNKNOWN status as a failure is cunho's fail-closed choice.

condition: Startup check in production; the identity proofing itself is the operator's duty (ARF-ISSU_18, EIDAS-2977-Art3(7))
quote: A PID Provider SHALL verify the identity of the subject of the PID in compliance with Level of Assurance (LoA) High requirements.
correction: The quoted duty binds the operator, as its own row says. This row is the software half that DESIGN.md §3 point 5 asks for: configuration that refuses to start when a required item is missing.

condition: Only if the issuer publishes credential_request_encryption; encryption on top of TLS is OPTIONAL
quote: jwks: REQUIRED. A JSON Web Key Set, as defined in [RFC7591], that contains one or more public keys, to be used by the Wallet as an input to a key agreement for encryption of the Credential Request. Each JWK in the set MUST have a kid (Key ID) parameter that uniquely identifies the key.
correction: §10 adds: "When encryption of a message was required but the received message is unencrypted, it SHOULD be rejected." HAIP 1.0's encryption clauses are for OpenID4VP responses only and add nothing here.

condition: Only if the issuer publishes credential_response_encryption and the wallet sends credential_response_encryption
quote: If the Client requested an encrypted response by including the credential_response_encryption object in the request, the Credential Issuer MUST encode the information in the Credential Response as specified by Section 10, using the parameters from the credential_response_encryption object.
correction: §9.2 says the same of the Deferred Credential Response, with the parameters of the deferred request. §8.3.1.2: Credential Error Responses are never encrypted.
